question: Should OpenClaw accept a permanent core AI-safety taxonomy with a public plugin emission API and durable operator history, or should the work be narrowed to existing diagnostics and external plugin seams first?
rationale: This changes core product scope, plugin SDK/manifest contracts, and persisted operator data; source review cannot safely choose the permanent ownership and API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
options.body: Approve a documented core taxonomy and require the branch to fix authoritative session identity, define the SDK contract, and prove upgrade/runtime behavior.

options.title: Keep diagnostics core-only
options.body: Retain only internal trusted diagnostics and defer plugin emission, durable history, and UI surfaces until a separately approved API design exists.

options.title: Route optional observability outward
options.body: Use the existing plugin/exporter seams for optional safety analytics and close or replace the broad core expansion.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
recommendation.body: Approve a documented core taxonomy and require the branch to fix authoritative session identity, define the SDK contract, and prove upgrade/runtime behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available low-confidence routing candidate for the cross-cutting product and plugin-contract decision.
